riders: You learn one of the following facts about the triggering effect, chosen by you: whether it was a spell, sphere talent, forged technique, item, innate feature, or monster action; whether the effect spent CP, a spell slot, item charges, or another limited resource; whether the creature can use the same effect again before the end of its next turn; whether the effect came from the creature's body, soul, weapon, item, Formation, or external patron.

You preserve one corpse, herb bundle, beast core, food supply, alchemical ingredient, fragile object, document, wound pattern, footprint, bloodstain, scent trace, or Small room. The subject does not rot, decay, spoil, dry out, mold, fade, or lose ordinary potency for the duration.
At CL 10, the duration becomes 7 days. At CL 15, the duration becomes 30 days.
Moonlit Preservation does not restore life, repair destroyed objects, halt a soul's departure, or prevent magical corruption unless another feature says so.
On a failed save, the repeated ability fails to activate, but the target does not spend CP, spell slots, charges, or limited uses for the failed attempt. The action used to attempt it is still spent.
On a successful save, the ability functions normally, but the target gains a Waning Mark after it resolves and cannot benefit from Advantage until the start of its next turn.
This does not prevent basic weapon attacks unless the attack is part of a named technique or special action.
On a failed save, the target cannot use the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again until the end of its next turn.
On a successful save, the target can repeat the ability, but if it does so before the end of its next turn, it gains a Waning Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.

riders: Until the start of its next turn, creatures more than 30 feet away cannot hear its voice unless it uses magical amplification or a cultivation technique with a higher CL than yours.
This does not prevent verbal components by itself.

You preserve its final state and draw one answer from the stillness. Ask the GM one question about the subject's final hour, final injury, final technique, final owner, final command, final emotion, final destination, or final visible enemy. The answer must be brief but truthful from the subject's available traces.
This does not speak with the dead, summon a soul, compel a spirit, or reveal information the subject left no trace of knowing.
